Subject: Re: Dedicated tenant - forensic deletion & replica sweep questions

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. As part of our procurement and security review we need a clear, auditable description of how Redwood will perform a forensic-ready deletion for a dedicated tenant in the EU region. Specifically, procurement/legal asked for: 

- A timeline for complete deletion across all replicas, snapshots, and backups (including cross-region copies if any) once the customer requests a termination or data purge.
- Evidence types you can provide (logs, checksums, snapshot manifests) and expected delivery format.
- Conditions for an emergency purge (e.g., legal hold lifted vs. court order) and SLA for completing an emergency sweep.
- Any limitations for immutable backups or third-party snapshot services.

We have a required case where a trial tenant will be decommissioned at contract termination and our risk/compliance team wants assurance that no residual data will remain and that we can receive verifiable proof. Can you put together the timeline and the artifacts we can expect? Also please confirm whether region pinning guarantees no cross-region replication for that dedicated pool.

Appreciate a short, clear answer for our security reviewers — Gina and I will map this into our contract redlines.

Best,
Evan
Security Architect, FinSecure

Laura — answering below, copying Karthik and Soojin for any infra/legal nuances. Long version condensed to the items FinSecure asked for.

1) Region pinning and cross-region replication
- For Dedicated pools we support "region pinning" which binds compute, primary storage, and object snapshots to the selected cloud region (we used eu-west-1 for this tenant). By default there is no asynchronous cross-region replication for tenant primary data or object snapshots when region-pin is enabled.
- Cross-region replication only occurs for explicit customer-requested DR replication profiles; we do not enable cross-region copies for tenants unless the customer subscribes to the multi-region replication add-on.

2) Normal termination deletion timeline (no legal hold)
- Day 0: Customer requests termination + confirmation of no legal hold. We generate a deletion ticket and schedule the purge in the maintenance window.
- Day 0–1: Quiesce access, revoke keys, revoke routing and API tokens. We snapshot the active KV cache (for forensic proving) and generate manifests/checksums.
- Day 1–3: Delete primary datasets (block/object layers) from serving nodes and mark blobs as deleted in metadata index. This triggers internal GC pipelines that free up in-cluster storage.
- Day 3–7: Background shard scrubbing and garbage-collection passes complete; snapshots expired and removed from storage tier.
- Day 7–14: Final metadata compaction and tombstone expiry; we produce final deletion attestations and logs.

Deliverable: within 14 days we provide a forensic package containing snapshot manifests, deletion logs, checksum proofs, and scrub-run logs. For standard terminations we include the sccm_export_manifest.xlsx and the snapshot manifest attachment shown earlier.

3) Emergency purge (forensic sweep) SLA
- Trigger: Security/legal escalation with documented authority (customer PO + signed directive) or court order.
- SLA: We can accelerate to a 72-hour targeted sweep for dedicated tenants in-region if compute/ops capacity is available. The 72-hr window includes snapshot removal and immediate background scrub priority.
- Evidence: We will provide time-stamped runbooks, purge job IDs, and scrub logs. For emergency purges we additionally provide a SHA256 manifest across removed blobs and an MD5 per-snapshot checksum.

4) Immutable backups / third-party services
- If the tenant opted into third-party immutable backup or vaulting (rare for trials), those backups are outside the regular Dedicated pool and are managed by the third-party provider. We will coordinate an export or deletion, but timelines depend on the third-party SLA. This is disclosed in the addendum.

5) Artifacts and formats we can provide
- Snapshot manifest (JSON + CSV) with blob IDs and sizes (example: tenant_snapshot_20280510.tar.gz).
- SCCM export (spreadsheet): sccm_export_manifest.xlsx with per-shard digest.
- Purge job logs: Redacted scrub logs with job IDs and timestamps (PDF/CSV).
- Final attestation: Signed statement from our infra team with run IDs and varnish of deletion steps (PDF).

6) Audit-friendly proofs and chain-of-custody
- We timestamp and sign all manifests using our internal key and provide checksums so your team can verify non-repudiation.
- Where required, we can arrange a live remote session to walk through the logs and manifests with an SRE.

Notes/Assumptions:
- The 14-day standard window assumes no legal hold and that the tenant is on a standard retention plan (no immutable vault enabled).
- Emergency 72-hour sweep is best-effort and requires coordination; extreme edge cases (hardware replacement, long-term cold archives) may extend timelines.

Attachments: redwood_purge_runbook_v2.pdf (internal runbook, redacted for external delivery) and the sample snapshot manifest FinSecure provided.

Happy to convert this into a 1-page letter for contractual inclusion.

Ben
Director, Storage & Ops
Redwood Inference

Evan / Gina — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise answer you can include in your security questionnaire; happy to sign off on a contractual attestation once you confirm the redlines.

Summary (short form for security review):
- Region pinning: Dedicated EU pool is region-pinned (eu-west-1). No cross-region replication is performed by default; cross-region replication is only enabled by explicit add-on.
- Standard deletion timeline: up to 14 days to produce a complete forensic package (snapshot manifests, deletion logs, checksums, scrub logs).
- Emergency purge SLA: 72-hour accelerated sweep (best-effort, requires documented authorization). Evidence delivered includes time-stamped purge run IDs, SHA256 manifests, and scrub logs.
- Immutable/third-party backups: If enabled, these are outside Redwood's standard deletion window; deletion coordinated with third-party provider per their SLA.
- Deliverables: tenant_snapshot_20280510.tar.gz (manifest), sccm_export_manifest.xlsx, redwood_purge_runbook_v2.pdf (redacted), and a signed deletion attestation.

Next steps:
1) Confirm whether FinSecure requires the 72-hour emergency SLA included in the contract (we can include as an exhibit).
2) If you want a write-up for the contract, we will prepare a one-page attestation and a stub clause specifying the evidence types (we can turn that around in 48 hours).
3) If you need a walkthrough of logs, propose a 30-minute SRE session — we have availability Friday 10:00–12:00 CET.

If this looks good I will attach the redacted runbook and the sample manifest to the contract package.

Thanks,
Laura
